lesson.title: Explain value before you trade on price
lesson.quick_idea: Before offering a concession, establish the concern and trade any approved concession for a defined scope or commitment.
lesson.why_it_matters: An early, unapproved discount answers a question the buyer did not ask, and makes the price the topic instead of the fit.
lesson.good_looks_like: You find the buyer’s real concern, connect the scope to it, and only then discuss a concession that is approved and traded for something.
lesson.better_direction: Ask what the team needs to see to trust the scope, show that value, and keep the list price until a trade is on the table.
example_wording: “Before we talk numbers, what would your team need to see to trust the scope?”
“If we can run one test case first, would that settle the fit question?”
lesson.when_to_use: When a buyer raises cost, scope or risk before a concession is approved.
lesson.when_not: A pre-authorised fixed promotion can be stated accurately without manufacturing a negotiation.
lesson.source: Synthetic sandbox lesson (synthetic-v1); owner’s Coaching specification §6.6.

media_clips.title: Objection: Answer Nahi, Diagnose
media_clips.reason: Dipak’s lesson on Certainty & Objection Intelligence, the skill you’re working on.
takeaways: Respond to the blocker and check resolution.
media_clips.transcript_excerpt: Prospect: “Mujhe sochna hai.” Bad: “Sure sir, kab call karun?” But “think” could mean price, value, spouse, fear, comparison, self-doubt, implementation, genuine processing, polite rejection. “Of course. Exactly kis part ke baare mein aapko sochna hai?” If prospect identifies something: diagnose it. If they genuinely need space: respect it. “Diagnosis ka goal har objection ko destroy karna nahi. Goal clarity create karna hai.”
